articles.title: DSP Mohammed Siraj Reports for Duty, Meets Telangana's New DGP CV Anand
articles.excerpt: India fast bowler Mohammed Siraj has officially donned the Telangana Police uniform as Deputy Superintendent of Police and met the state's newly appointed Director General of Police, CV Anand, in Hyderabad — balancing his dual roles as cricketer and police officer.
articles.image_caption: DSP Mohammed Siraj reported for duty and met Telangana's new Director General of Police, CV Anand (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Siraj's appointment reflects a long tradition of Indian state governments honouring athletes with government posts, a system that resonates strongly with diaspora communities who closely follow Indian cricket and take pride in players' off-field recognition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Renames School Breakfast Scheme After Kamaraj, Expands Coverage to 35 Lakh Students
articles.excerpt: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's TVK government honours the late Congress leader who pioneered India's school meals movement, while extending breakfast to middle school students at an additional cost of ₹343 crore.
articles.image_caption: Children eat breakfast at a government primary school under Tamil Nadu's state-funded breakfast programme. The scheme, now renamed after former Chief Minister K. Kamaraj, is being expanded to cover students through Class 8.
articles.image_credit: The Hindu Business Line / Venkatachalapathy C
articles.nri_angle: Tamil Nadu's school meals programme, one of India's oldest welfare initiatives, continues to serve as a benchmark for child nutrition policy nationwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sri Lanka Deploys Air Force Drones as Worst Dengue Outbreak in a Decade Kills 53
articles.excerpt: With more than 76,000 infections and hospitals comparing the surge to COVID-era peaks, the island nation has mobilised its military to hunt mosquito-breeding sites using drone surveillance.
articles.image_caption: Aedes mosquitoes, the primary vector for dengue fever. Sri Lanka is battling its worst outbreak in a decade (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The outbreak is directly relevant to the Sri Lankan and South Asian diaspora with family ties in the worst-affected regions around Colombo and Negombo.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jim Jordan Asks DOJ to Prosecute Jack Smith Over Alleged Congressional Perjury
articles.excerpt: The House Judiciary Committee chairman accuses the former special counsel of misleading lawmakers about accessing text messages from 44 members of Congress during his Trump investigations.
articles.image_caption: Former Special Counsel Jack Smith during his tenure leading the investigations into President Donald Trump. Jordan alleges Smith misled Congress about accessing lawmakers' text messages during his probes.
articles.nri_angle: The referral intensifies the ongoing partisan battle over the Justice Department's independence, a debate that has resonated with Indian-American political observers following the community's growing engagement in U.S. politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Omar Abdullah Fact-Checks JP Nadda Over JKSSB Paper Leak Timeline
articles.excerpt: The J&K Chief Minister corrected the BJP leader's claim about the JKSSB paper leak date, pointing out it occurred under LG administration — not his government — as the NEET controversy roils Parliament.
articles.image_caption: Omar Abdullah serves as the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir. He publicly corrected JP Nadda's claims about the JKSSB paper leak timeline during the ongoing NEET controversy.
articles.nri_angle: Examination integrity concerns affect millions of Indian families worldwide whose children pursue competitive exams as pathways to careers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lohagad Fort Murder: Accused Initially Planned to Injure Fiancé, Not Kill, Say Police
articles.excerpt: Pune police reveal Siya Goyal and her boyfriend first researched ways to disable Ketan Agarwal before escalating their conspiracy to murder at the Maharashtra hill fort.
articles.image_caption: Lohagad Fort near Pune, Maharashtra, where 26-year-old Ketan Agarwal was allegedly pushed to his death on June 18. Police have arrested his fiancée Siya Goyal and her boyfriend Chetan Chaudhary for the murder.
articles.nri_angle: The case has drawn intense attention from the Indian diaspora, particularly among Marwari and business communities, as both families are prominent Pune-based business families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Declares Iran Ceasefire 'Over' as US Strikes Enter 12th Night and Hormuz Tanker Traffic Stalls
articles.excerpt: The president's announcement at a NATO summit in Turkey came as CENTCOM confirmed strikes on more than 80 Iranian targets and oil tankers reversed course in the Red Sea after Houthi threats.
articles.image_caption: A satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to the Arabian Sea. The strait carries roughly one-fifth of the world's oil trade.
articles.nri_angle: Rising oil prices from the Hormuz crisis are pushing up fuel and commodity costs globally, directly affecting Indian diaspora households and remittance-dependent families in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US House Passes Sweeping Restrictions on Lawmaker Stock Trading
articles.excerpt: The 'Stop Insider Trading Act' cleared the House 232-198, barring lawmakers and their families from buying new stocks while in office, though a voter ID provision attached to the bill drew fierce Democratic opposition.
articles.image_caption: The US House of Representatives chamber during a legislative session in Washington, DC. The House voted 232-198 on Wednesday to pass the Stop Insider Trading Act, restricting lawmakers and their families from purchasing new stocks while in office.
articles.nri_angle: Indian American lawmakers like Rep. Ro Khanna are among the top congressional stock traders, and the reforms could reshape how NRI investors track congressional stock disclosures as market signals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Experimental Ebola Vaccines Race Ahead as Congo Death Toll Nears 1,000
articles.excerpt: With no approved treatments for the Bundibugyo strain, Africa CDC is preparing a cross-protection trial for health workers while developers including Oxford and Serum Institute of India push toward clinical trials.
articles.image_caption: Health workers from Médecins Sans Frontières respond to the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. At least 121 frontline responders have been infected during the crisis, with 36 deaths.
articles.nri_angle: India's Serum Institute is developing one of the leading Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine candidates with Oxford, extending their COVID-19 partnership, while the Indian diaspora in East Africa faces direct exposure risks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: House Passes $95 Billion Budget Framework for Iran War and Election Overhaul
articles.excerpt: The budget resolution cleared the House 216-214, funding defense spending for the Middle East conflict and Trump's SAVE America Act, but faces an uncertain path in the Senate.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol building in Washington, D.C. House Republicans passed a $95 billion budget framework on Wednesday in a 216-214 vote to fund defense spending for the Iran war and election reforms.
articles.nri_angle: The defense spending and voter ID provisions carry implications for Indian Americans — Gulf-deployed military operations affect oil prices and Indian workers in the region, while new voter registration requirements could impact naturalized citizens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Daniel Siad, Model Scout Named 2,000 Times in Epstein Files, Found Dead in France
articles.excerpt: The 69-year-old French modeling recruiter, who was under investigation for allegedly helping Jeffrey Epstein traffic young women across Europe, was discovered dead at his home near Paris. French prosecutors say the broader probe will continue.
articles.image_caption: Daniel Siad during a CNN interview in June 2026. The French modeling scout was found dead at his home near Paris on Monday while under investigation for his alleged role in Jeffrey Epstein's trafficking network.
articles.nri_angle: The case highlights how Epstein's trafficking network spanned continents, with Siad recruiting women from across Europe, North Africa, and beyond — underscoring the global reach of sex trafficking operations that advocacy groups in diaspora communities have long warned about.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's 'Cockroach' Youth Protests Force Parliament Shutdown, Draw Celebrity Support
articles.excerpt: Thousands of Gen Z protesters demanding the education minister's resignation over the NEET exam paper leak have clashed with police in Delhi, shut down metro stations, and drawn backing from Bollywood stars and opposition leaders.
articles.image_caption: Protesters gather at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi during the Cockroach Janta Party's ongoing demonstrations against the NEET paper leak. The site, a historic observatory turned protest ground, has been the movement's headquarters since June 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The NEET scandal and youth unemployment crisis resonate deeply with diaspora families whose children face similar examination pressures, while solidarity rallies in London, New York, and San Jose show the movement's global reach
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Threatens to Destroy Iranian Infrastructure as US-Iran War Escalates
articles.excerpt: The U.S. president vowed to bomb a bridge or power plant for every Iranian attack on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Tehran to warn it would target regional energy facilities and block all oil exports.
articles.image_caption: U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump has threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure as the U.S.-Iran military conflict escalates.
articles.nri_angle: Indian energy consumers face rising fuel costs as dual threats to the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping lanes endanger crude oil imports
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Attends Dignified Transfer of Four U.S. Soldiers Killed in Iran War
articles.excerpt: The ceremony at Dover Air Force Base came as the U.S. death toll in Iran rose to 18, with growing bipartisan opposition and surging oil prices threatening India's energy security.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth salute during the dignified transfer of four fallen U.S. service members at Dover Air Force Base on July 22, 2026. The ceremony marked the return of soldiers killed in Iranian attacks in Jordan and Iraq.
articles.image_credit: SAUL LOEB / AFP via Getty Images
articles.nri_angle: India's crude oil import bill surged 60% as the Strait of Hormuz closure disrupted traditional Middle East supply routes, forcing Indian refiners to pivot to Russian and Latin American crude. The dual chokepoint crisis threatens inflation and energy security for the world's third-largest oil importer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Heat Accidentally Post LeBron James Press Conference Link, Fueling Return Speculation
articles.excerpt: Miami's social media department mistakenly published a YouTube livestream for a 'LeBron James Introductory Press Conference,' sending prediction markets and NBA fans into overdrive as the 41-year-old's free agency decision looms.
articles.image_caption: LeBron James during a game for the Los Angeles Lakers. The four-time NBA champion is currently an unrestricted free agent weighing offers from the Miami Heat, Philadelphia 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Golden State Warriors.
articles.nri_angle: NBA has a growing following among the Indian diaspora, with LeBron James among the league's most recognized global figures.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's 'Cockroach' Youth Protests Erupt Into Biggest Challenge to Modi in a Decade
articles.excerpt: Tens of thousands of young Indians are demanding education reforms and the resignation of the education minister after NEET exam paper leaks affected 2 million students. Police tear gas and baton charges have only hardened their resolve.
articles.image_caption: Police fire tear gas at Cockroach Janta Party supporters during the 'Chalo Sansad' march in New Delhi on July 20, 2026. The clashes left over 150 protesters hospitalized, according to CJP leaders.
articles.nri_angle: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke is a Boston University graduate; NEET affects millions of Indian families including those in the diaspora planning medical education; youth unemployment driving protests is a concern frequently cited by diaspora communities
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Approves 30-Year Nuclear Deal Allowing Saudi Arabia to Enrich Uranium
articles.excerpt: The landmark agreement, worth tens of billions of dollars, would give American companies a central role in Saudi Arabia's nuclear program while opening the door to uranium enrichment on Saudi soil under a secretive arrangement.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump approved a landmark 30-year nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia that allows Riyadh to enrich uranium.
articles.nri_angle: Implications for the 2.5 million Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia and India's own nuclear cooperation history with the US; regional stability concerns affect Gulf diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NEET Paper Leaked Thrice in Five Years, Yet No One Has Been Held Accountable: K. Annamalai
articles.excerpt: The former BJP Tamil Nadu chief's sharp criticism of the Centre comes as a CBI probe reveals insider involvement, student suicides mount, and tens of thousands march on Parliament.
articles.image_caption: K. Annamalai, BJP leader and former IPS officer, called for accountability over repeated NEET paper leaks.

sources.label: The Hindu — CBI arrests in NEET leak

articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora families funding NEET coaching for children and relatives back home are directly affected — the exam's integrity determines medical college admissions that shape career trajectories across continents.

articles.title: US Faces Largest Cyclosporiasis Outbreak on Record With Over 11,500 Cases Across 41 States
articles.excerpt: The CDC has linked the parasitic outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, with Michigan reporting over 7,000 cases alone. No deaths have been reported.
articles.image_caption: Microscopic view of Cyclospora cayetanensis, the parasite behind the largest cyclosporiasis outbreak in U.S. history with over 11,500 cases.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans who regularly consume fresh produce should follow CDC guidance on washing and cooking vegetables to reduce cyclospora exposure risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Methane Blast at Sikkim Hydropower Tunnel Kills 20, Five Workers Still Missing
articles.excerpt: A suspected methane gas explosion inside an under-construction tunnel at the NHPC's Teesta Stage-VI project in Namchi district trapped 25 workers on Monday. Rescue teams have recovered 20 bodies, with five workers still unaccounted for.
articles.image_caption: Rescue teams work at the site of the tunnel blast at the NHPC Teesta Stage-VI Hydroelectric Project in Sikkim's Namchi district. Twenty bodies have been recovered from the methane-filled tunnel, with five workers still missing.
articles.nri_angle: The tragedy raises safety questions about India's ambitious hydropower expansion in the Himalayas, a region where diaspora families have roots and where the 2023 Uttarkashi tunnel collapse drew global attention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tate Brothers Face 59 Charges as Unsealed Documents Detail Rape Allegations
articles.excerpt: Andrew and Tristan Tate appeared in a Miami federal court in handcuffs and shackles as newly released filings revealed harrowing accounts from seven women spanning 2010 to 2017.
articles.image_caption: Andrew Tate at a public appearance prior to his arrest. The social media influencer and his brother Tristan now face a combined 59 criminal charges in the UK as they fight extradition from US custody.
articles.nri_angle: The case has drawn attention from Indian diaspora audiences given the Tate brothers' large online following in South Asia and the involvement of UK and US legal systems familiar to many NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mega Millions Jackpot Soars to $743 Million After No Winner in Tuesday Drawing
articles.excerpt: The prize, now the 10th largest in Mega Millions history, rolls to Friday as both major U.S. lotteries top $500 million simultaneously.
articles.image_caption: A Mega Millions lottery ticket; the jackpot has grown to $743 million
articles.nri_angle: Non-U.S. citizens on work or student visas can legally buy Mega Millions and Powerball tickets and claim prizes, though they face a 30% federal tax withholding compared to 24% for citizens and permanent residents.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICMR Licenses Three Indigenous Biomedical Technologies to Emcure, Biological E
articles.excerpt: India's premier medical research body transfers a novel cervical cancer therapy and two next-generation enteric vaccine technologies to domestic pharmaceutical manufacturers under its Patent Mitra initiative.
articles.image_caption: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), which licensed three biomedical technologies
articles.nri_angle: The technology transfers highlight India's growing shift from generic drug manufacturing toward indigenous biomedical innovation, relevant for diaspora healthcare professionals and investors tracking the country's pharmaceutical sector.
